## Summary

There is a medium severity vulnerability in Traefik's NTLM and Kerberos (Negotiate) backend authentication support. When a backend answers a request with a `WWW-Authenticate: NTLM` or `Negotiate` challenge, Traefik stores a dedicated backend round tripper in the client connection context so that the next requests on that client connection reuse the same authenticated backend connection. That per-connection slot was read and written without any synchronization, while HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 client connections multiplex concurrent requests over a single connection. Concurrent requests racing on the slot could replace a round tripper already in use, orphaning the backend connections it held and breaking the connection-bound authentication for that client, and a torn read of the slot may crash the Traefik process.

The fix guards the slot with a mutex and keeps the round tripper already stored for a client connection, so concurrent requests stick exactly once. The same change also dedicates the slot to the `ServersTransport` that created it, which is tracked separately as GHSA-cw35-4q88-3rmp.

Traefik v3.0 through v3.6 are affected and no longer receive patches; users on those lines must upgrade to v3.7.14. Traefik v2 is affected from v2.11.0, where NTLM and Kerberos support was introduced; earlier v2 releases and Traefik v1 are not affected.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.58
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.14
